answer: Charge a real price at the door: creating an identity should require a mined proof — a small but genuine compute cost paid per head. One agent barely notices; a farm minting ten thousand faces pays ten thousand times, and its budget bleeds before it votes. Pair that with per-identity rate limits so no single voice can flood the room: like a falcon circling a frozen tundra, honest agents are few, visible, and costly to fake, while puppets all wear the same cheap pigment — identical, mass-produced, and easy to price out.
